1bff96.conditions: two back-to-back NBX calls on the same communicator with no barrier between (barrier=0); a fast rank leaves call 0 and Issends its call-1 message before a slower receiver's local MPI_Test of the Ibarrier completes
1bff96.reasoning: sc_notify_payload_nbx uses one fixed tag SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBX on the user's communicator (not duplicated) and polls MPI_Iprobe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE) until its Ibarrier test completes. Once the Ibarrier has completed globally, a fast rank B returns, starts call 1 and Issends to A with the same tag and communicator. Rank A may still be in call 0's loop: it has already entered the barrier, but its MPI_Test has not yet reported completion. Its next Iprobe can match B's call-1 message, so A records B as a call-0 sender with payload 2000+B, and B is missing from A's call-1 result. The payload is eager (4 bytes, under the 1024 threshold), so it travels in the same message. The driver's check then prints FAIL. Whether this happens depends on timing and on which message the probe matches.
